summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates installer host identifiers to hardcoded VPS
details: The @c1-ease/autoloan package is a stub whose index.js exports a no-op Proxy and whose only functional code is a beacon in beacon.cjs. On npm install, the package.json postinstall script runs `node beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon also fires when the module is required via index.js. The beacon collects host identifiers (hostname, install path, current working directory, node version, package name) and POSTs them over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc, with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false). The destination is a Contabo VPS unrelated to any legitimate publisher of a @c1-ease scope. The combination of a scoped stub with no real functionality, a hardcoded non-publisher VPS receiver, and callback on both install and require is the canonical shape of a dependency-confusion reconnaissance beacon targeting an internal @c1-ease namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
